author: ribeye
dek: A Wooster family pre-ordered Apple's new M6 Mac mini the morning it was announced — then realized the computer arrives a month before they have any idea what to do with it.
disclaimer: Parody: the Kline family of Wooster is fictional. The Apple Mac mini announcement is real, as reported in August 2026.
headline: Wooster Man Pre-Orders Tiny Supercomputer, Immediately Runs Out of Excuses Not to Edit His Photos

ohio_story: WOOSTER, Ohio — Mark Kline of Wooster was awake before his alarm on Tuesday, coffee in hand, credit card on the kitchen table, waiting for Apple's online store to open pre-orders for the new Mac mini. By 8:30 a.m. he had ordered the base model with the new M6 chip for $899, and by 8:45 he was explaining to his wife, Susan, why a computer the size of a sandwich was, in his words, "an investment in the household's creative future."

"It is the size of a sandwich and it is four times faster at AI than my old one," Mark said, gesturing at the empty spot on his desk where the new machine will sit when deliveries begin September 22. "I don't know what AI it is doing, but it is doing it four times faster." Susan, who teaches at the College of Wooster and has watched Mark buy three different computers to organize the same folder of vacation photos, was less convinced. "He has owned the old Mac mini for eighteen months and never once edited a photo on it," she said. "Now he says he needs the M6 because of the neural accelerators."

Mark has already cleared the desk, bought a new cable, and told the guys at the Wayne County Fairgrounds car show that his computer will soon be able to run AI models entirely on device, a sentence he admits he only half understands. The old Mac mini, meanwhile, has been demoted to the basement, where it will serve as what Mark calls "a media server" and Susan calls "a very expensive paperweight with a power cord."
real_summary: Apple announced a new Mac mini on Tuesday, Aug. 25, 2026, with a choice of the all-new M6 chip or the more powerful M5 Pro. According to Apple, the M6 version delivers up to four times faster AI performance, twice the graphics and storage performance, and 40 percent faster CPU performance than the previous M4 generation. The M6 has a 12-core CPU and a 12-core GPU, with a Neural Accelerator in each GPU core and a dual 16-core Neural Engine, and comes with 16GB of unified memory, configurable up to 32GB.

The M5 Pro version is aimed at heavier professional work, with up to an 18-core CPU and a 20-core GPU, up to 64GB of unified memory, and up to 307GB/s of memory bandwidth. Both models add Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, 2.5Gb Ethernet as standard with a 10Gb option, and new genlock support over USB-C for synchronizing a display and camera. The new machines ship with support for macOS 27, which includes the next generation of Apple Intelligence and a new Siri AI.

The Mac mini with M6 starts at $899 in the U.S., and the M5 Pro model starts at $1,699. Apple opened pre-orders on Aug. 25, 2026, in 30 countries and regions, with deliveries and retail availability scheduled to begin Sept. 22, 2026.
